messages:
jen: heads-up — on-call had a customer incident where Dedicated tenant hit our p99 SLO and the fallback flow just started dropping requests. Can we align on a safer degradation playbook?
raj: ugh. which fallback kicked in? model downgrade or hard 429?
jen: hard 429s from the admission service. the tenant was on a heavy reranking workload + embeddings batch.
maya: that sounds like the admission layer had no soft-shed path. we discussed 'graceful degrade -> variant downgrade -> queueing -> drop' but never formalized order.
dan: +1. proposal: prefer model-variant downgrade first (quantized or smaller model), then enable per-tenant burst window queueing for 30s, then sample-based soft-shed (return partial results), and only as last resort 429.
sara: can we make the queueing per-route not per-tenant? some tenants are fine with longer latencies on embeddings but not on chat.
raj: good call. route-specific degrade policies make sense. we should own per-route priorities in the admission policy.
jen: ops-bot posted metrics: "cpu_gpu_util: 94%", "admission_drop_rate: 2.6%" — customer SLA is 99.9% p99 latency. When GPU pressure spikes, current strategy is binary.
maya: tradeoff: model-variant downgrade preserves throughput but might change output quality. need a way to tie a small set of canary prompts that we evaluate quickly before downgrading broadly.
dan: maybe a hysteresis rule: only downgrade a tenant after N requests or if global util > T for M seconds, and rollback when util drops. avoid flip-flopping.
raj: add telemetry: per-tenant degrade-events with reasons (cpu|mem|kvcache) + variant-id + sampled prompt/score. must be surfaced in console.
sara: SLA scenarios to document: (1) transient spike <1m -> queue+variant, (2) sustained >5m -> throttle+notify sales, (3) abuse pattern -> immediate probation.
jen: for abuse detection, we should not conflate legitimate bursts. suggestion: require an 'abuse score' threshold derived from request patterns, errors, and billing anomalies before punitive evictions.
maya: also preserve graceful fallback for private deployments — customers running private infra may prefer controlled 429s vs silent output drift. add a deployment-level preference flag: `degrade_preference: [variant|latency|drop]`.
dan: implementation sketch: admission service config: `route_policy = {priority:int, variant_preferences:[], queue_budget_ms:int, soft_shed_rate:float, abuse_threshold:int}`. admission evaluates in order and emits debug headers like `x-redwood-degrade: variant=v2-q, reason=util-spike`.
raj: ops concern: queueing adds memory pressure. keep per-tenant queue size bounded and backpressure to edge. maybe implement token-bucket that pads requests into the serving pool instead of long in-process queues.
sara: can we do progressive ramping? when we detect pressure, start by applying to low-priority tenants only (10% sample), then expand. gives us time to observe quality regressions.
jen: yes, rollout plan: canary on internal tenants -> opt-in customers -> global. need a playbook for rollback that includes clearing queued requests and notifying customers.
maya: test harness idea: synthetic workload runner that mimics mixed workloads (chat + rerank + embeddings) and can toggle variant downgrades to measure p99/quality delta.
dan: tie to billing: when variant downgrade happens, mark the request at actual variant pricing and include in cost breakdown so customers see transparency.
raj: open question: do we provide a 'degrade-as-a-service' API so customers can opt into behavior per-tenant? I think yes — add `degrade_profile_id` to tenant config.
sara: ops runbook snippets: `# to escalate: run make drain-tenant TENANT_ID=xyz; set degrade_lock=on; notify-sales` — keep short.
jen: action items: (1) eng-platform write RFC with ordered degrade states + API (2) eng-runtime implement variant headers and lightweight canary evaluator (3) eng-infra add synthetic workload tests and memory-safe queue implementation (4) product/ops draft customer-facing documentation and billing transparency.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-5632: "Degrade playbook RFC + test harness" assigned to eng-platform. :white_check_mark:
raj: i'll take the RFC. will post draft in 48h.
maya: i'll sketch the canary evaluator and sample prompt set.
dan: i'll prototype queue/token-bucket options.
sara: i'll coordinate runbook and customer comms.
jen: thanks team — let's try to avoid surprise 429s next time. :thumbsup:
